title: Amrita Puri Has No Regrets About Leaving Bollywood for a Master's
excerpt: The Aisha and Kai Po Che actor says she stepped away for two years to study at the University of Edinburgh, knew the industry might forget her, and would make the same choice again.
body:
• Amrita Puri said she has no regrets about pausing her film career for two years to complete a master's degree at the University of Edinburgh, in an interview on The Shaili Chopra Show.
  • She acknowledged the break may have cost her roles and that people assumed she had quit acting or left the country — and said she accepted the risk of being forgotten.
  • Puri also said her parents initially did not want her to become an actor, and that knowing the profession was unreliable shaped both decisions: to enter it, and to leave it temporarily.
  • The actor, who made her Hindi debut in the 2010 film Aisha, was most recently seen in the series IC 814: The Kandahar Hijack.

Actor Amrita Puri has said she has no regrets about taking a two-year break from films to complete a master's degree in the United Kingdom, even though the absence led people in the industry to assume she had stopped acting altogether, according to The Times of India's account of her interview on The Shaili Chopra Show.

"If people forget me in the film business, I will come back and take it from there. It's these things that build your confidence and give you a sense of identity."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Wdm466yrGPs — Amrita Puri, actor

"You Can't Have Everything"

Puri made her Hindi film debut in Aisha (2010), playing a supporting role alongside Sonam Kapoor that earned her a Filmfare nomination for Best Supporting Actress. After a handful of projects, she paused acting and moved to the UK for her master's at the University of Edinburgh.

"I stepped away and I did my masters. I moved and went to a different country. I was unavailable for two years and people were like, 'She is not acting anymore.' 'Does she even live here anymore?' It's a choice and it is true, you can't have everything in life," she said. She admitted she is "the queen" of wondering "what if," and that the break may have cost her a few film roles — but said the answer, for her, is to trust her own judgement about what is meant to come her way.

Two Decisions Against the Odds

The interview linked the study break to an earlier decision made on the same terms. Puri said her parents did not want her to become an actor when she started, and that she understood their reasoning: she knew before entering that acting was an unreliable profession in which she might fail, and chose it anyway. The master's, she suggested, followed the same logic in reverse — she would go even if she was the oldest person in the classroom.

"Decisions that I have taken have made me who I am," she said, as Zoom TV's account of the conversation also reported. Both outlets noted her framing of the two choices — acting against her parents' wishes, and education against the industry's momentum — as the experiences that built her confidence and identity.

The Work Before and After

After Aisha, Puri appeared in Blood Money (2012) and gained wider recognition in the 2013 sports drama Kai Po Che, alongside Rajkummar Rao and Sushant Singh Rajput. She later featured in Judgementall Hai Kya and built a substantial streaming career with Four More Shots Please!, Made in Heaven, Mentalhood and Jeet Ki Zid. Her most recent credit is Anubhav Sinha's series IC 814: The Kandahar Hijack, in an ensemble cast including Vijay Varma, Naseeruddin Shah, Pankaj Kapur, Dia Mirza and Arvind Swamy.

Puri did not announce a new project in the interview. Its point was narrower and, for an industry that treats absence as disappearance, pointed: a two-year education break is a choice she defends on its own terms, not a gap she feels she has to explain away.
